concepts.name: What Software Architecture Is
concepts.notes: Design vs architecture, behaviour vs structure as the two values of software, architecture's goals (facilitate development, deployment, operation, maintenance), keeping options open. Clean Architecture book summary is the primary source; architecture-styles adds the 'styles as constraints' framing.

concepts.name: Programming Paradigms as Architectural Tools
concepts.notes: Structured programming, OO (encapsulation/inheritance/polymorphism, dependency inversion as OO's architectural superpower), functional immutability and event sourcing. Single source but coherent treatment.

concepts.name: SOLID Design Principles
concepts.notes: SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP from the book summary; modern-web-apps' 'Architectural principles' adds separation of concerns, encapsulation, explicit dependencies, DRY, persistence ignorance, bounded contexts. Some SRP subsections in the summary are placeholder-thin (1-9 words) — synthesis happens at exercise/objective level, content stays source-faithful.

concepts.name: Component Principles
concepts.notes: Component cohesion (REP, CCP, CRP), the tension diagram, coupling (ADP, SDP, SAP), stability and abstraction metrics. Single source, summary-level depth.

concepts.name: Layers, Boundaries, and Policy
concepts.notes: Vertical/horizontal layers, decoupling modes, drawing boundary lines, boundary anatomy and crossing, policy and level, business rules (entities vs use cases), screaming architecture, plugin architecture.

concepts.name: The Clean Architecture Pattern
concepts.notes: The concentric-circles model, Dependency Rule, the four layers, crossing boundaries, Humble Object, partial boundaries, when (not) to use it, web application example with sample code. modern-web-apps gives the ASP.NET Core organization of the same pattern — strong two-source coverage.

concepts.name: Architectural Details: Database, Web, Frameworks
concepts.notes: 'The database is a detail', 'the web is a detail', frameworks as an asymmetric marriage, package-by-layer/feature/component strategies, case study. Distinctive Clean Architecture material rounding out the book.

concepts.name: Monoliths, Layered (N-tier) Architecture
concepts.notes: All-in-one apps, what layers are, traditional N-layer apps, monoliths in containers; N-tier style page with when-to-use/benefits/challenges. Good two-source coverage with different vocabularies (DDD-flavoured vs ops-flavoured).

concepts.name: Architecture Styles Catalog
concepts.notes: The tour of styles (N-tier, Web-Queue-Worker, Microservices, Event-driven, Big data, Big compute), styles as constraints, challenge/benefit trade-off thinking. Big data and big compute are out of scope for a web-focused curriculum — referenced only in the overview.

concepts.name: Event-Driven Architecture
concepts.notes: Pub/sub vs event streaming, consumer patterns, when to use, challenges (1021w architecture section + 920w challenges). The system-design-primer asynchronism sections complement it.

concepts.name: Web-Queue-Worker Architecture
concepts.notes: Simple cloud-native style bridging monoliths and microservices; pairs naturally with background-jobs best practices from api-best-practices.json.

concepts.name: Microservices Fundamentals
concepts.notes: What microservices are, components, benefits/challenges/best practices/antipatterns. Clean Architecture's 'Services: Great and Small' provides a valuable critical counterpoint (decoupling hype, services by functional decomposition pitfall).

concepts.name: Domain Analysis and DDD for Microservices
concepts.notes: Strategic DDD (domain analysis, bounded contexts), tactical DDD (entities, value objects, aggregates, domain services/events), drone-delivery worked example, microservice boundary derivation. modern-web-apps adds 'should you apply DDD?'.

concepts.name: Interservice Communication
concepts.notes: Sync vs async messaging trade-offs, service mesh, distributed transactions/saga, RPC vs REST comparison, message encoding formats (JSON, Protobuf, Avro...) from api-best-practices message-encode sections.

concepts.name: API Gateways
concepts.notes: Gateway routing/aggregation/offloading, options and technology choice. Single source but focused treatment; reverse-proxy sections in system-design-primer are adjacent.

concepts.name: RESTful API Design
concepts.notes: Resource URIs, HTTP methods semantics, pagination/filtering, partial responses, HATEOAS, maturity model, OpenAPI; microservices-design adds REST-to-DDD mapping and idempotency; three-source coverage.

concepts.name: API Versioning and Evolution
concepts.notes: No/URI/query/header/media-type versioning trade-offs from both sources.

concepts.name: Web API Implementation Practices
concepts.notes: Idempotent processing, exception handling, client-side caching with ETags, optimistic concurrency, large payloads, async long-running requests, statelessness, throttling, API documentation/SDKs, testing and monitoring a web API. Azure API Management subsections are vendor-specific — referenced selectively.

concepts.name: HTTP and Web Protocols
concepts.notes: HTTP, TCP, UDP, RPC, REST fundamentals — the communication groundwork for API design and distributed systems topics.

concepts.name: Modern Web Application Architecture
concepts.notes: Characteristics of modern web apps, traditional server-rendered vs SPA decision, Blazor, client-side technology landscape (HTML/CSS/JS, Angular/React/Vue), choosing a SPA framework. Web-only scope per user requirement — no native mobile.

concepts.name: Server-Side Web Implementation Patterns (ASP.NET Core)
concepts.notes: MVC and Razor Pages, request routing/filters, dependency injection in practice, feature organization, cross-cutting concerns, security (Identity, authn/authz), deployment. Framework-specific but illustrates the general patterns; treated as the curriculum's concrete implementation case study.

concepts.name: Data Access and Persistence in Web Apps
concepts.notes: EF Core patterns, repository/encapsulation, micro-ORMs, SQL vs NoSQL decision (both sources), NoSQL store types, response/data caching in the app tier.

concepts.name: Testing Web Applications
concepts.notes: Unit/integration/functional tests, testing pyramid, organizing and naming tests; Clean Architecture's test boundary and design-for-testability sections give the architectural rationale.

concepts.name: Scalability Fundamentals
concepts.notes: Performance vs scalability, latency vs throughput, CAP theorem, consistency patterns, availability patterns and the 9s, fail-over modes.

concepts.name: Web Infrastructure Building Blocks
concepts.notes: DNS, CDNs (primer + cdn-content best practices), load balancers L4/L7, reverse proxies, horizontal scaling, application-layer separation and service discovery.

concepts.name: Database Scaling and Partitioning
prerequisites: Data Access and Persistence in Web Apps
concepts.notes: Replication (master-slave/master-master), federation, sharding, denormalization, SQL tuning from the primer; horizontal/vertical/functional partitioning design from best practices.

concepts.name: Caching Strategies
concepts.notes: Cache levels (client, CDN, web server, database, application), update patterns (cache-aside, write-through, write-behind, refresh-ahead), expiration/invalidation, concurrency, eventual consistency. Azure Managed Redis subsections are vendor-specific — used selectively for the cache-aside implementation example.

concepts.name: Asynchronous Processing and Message Queues
concepts.notes: Message queues, task queues, back pressure from the primer; background-jobs best practices (triggers, idempotency, partitioning, coordination, reliability) from best practices.

concepts.name: The Twelve-Factor Methodology
concepts.notes: All 12 factors with full original text. Note: extraction kept the descriptive taglines as section titles (e.g. 'One codebase tracked in revision control, many deploys' = Codebase); topics will restore the canonical factor names.

concepts.name: Deployment and Delivery for Distributed Systems
concepts.notes: CI/CD for microservices, monorepo vs multirepo, rolling/blue-green/canary releases, GitOps; container orchestration advantages; 12factor build-release-run underpins it.

concepts.name: Resilience and Transient Fault Handling
concepts.notes: Why transient faults occur, retry strategies/intervals, antipatterns, circuit-breaker adjacency, testing retry logic. Single source but thorough.

concepts.name: Monitoring and Observability
prerequisites: Deployment and Delivery for Distributed Systems
concepts.notes: Health/availability/performance/security/SLA monitoring, instrumentation, the monitoring pipeline, hot/warm/cold analysis, dashboards and alerting; distributed tracing appears in API best practices and compute-options observability.

concepts.name: Autoscaling
concepts.notes: Autoscaling components and design considerations; the Azure Monitor walkthrough is vendor-specific and used selectively.

concepts.name: Microservices Data Management
prerequisites: Domain Analysis and DDD for Microservices
concepts.notes: Database-per-service, polyglot persistence, eventual consistency challenges, drone-delivery data store choices.

concepts.name: Microservices Compute and Orchestration
prerequisites: Deployment and Delivery for Distributed Systems
concepts.notes: Container orchestration rationale and platform decision factors (interservice communication, independent scaling/deployability, observability, state). Azure platform comparisons are vendor-specific — the decision factors generalize.

gaps.concept: Web security architecture (OWASP-style threat modeling, OAuth2/OIDC flows in depth)
gaps.suggestion: Sources cover authentication/authorization in ASP.NET Core, API throttling, and cache data protection, but there is no dedicated security-architecture source. A source like the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series (github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries) would fill this.
gaps.resolution: user_accepted: network allowlist constrains sources to verified GitHub repos; security is covered at moderate depth via modern-web-apps Security sections and API best practices (throttling, protecting cached data). Flagged for a future curriculum iteration.

gaps.concept: Architecture documentation and decision records (C4 model, ADRs)
gaps.suggestion: Could add joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record or the C4 model docs as a small supplementary source.
Mentioned in compute options and background-jobs hosting but not treated as a style. Azure Architecture Center has a serverless section that could be added.
Both are mentioned (generic data access APIs, RPC) but not covered in depth. Official graphql.github.io / grpc.io docs repos could supplement.

concept_order: Data Access and Persistence in Web Apps
Domain Analysis and DDD for Microservices
Deployment and Delivery for Distributed Systems
coverage_summary: Seven GitHub-hosted sources give strong, multi-perspective coverage of the requested scope: principles (SOLID, component principles), Clean Architecture, architectural styles, microservices (design, DDD, communication, data, CI/CD), web implementation technologies (ASP.NET Core as the concrete stack, SPA-vs-traditional, client-side landscape), API design/implementation, scalability building blocks (caching, partitioning, queues, CDNs, load balancing), and cloud-native operations (twelve-factor, resilience, monitoring, autoscaling). Microsoft sources carry some Azure-specific subsections which are used selectively; system-design-primer carries interview-prep meta sections which are deliberately not mapped into topics. Total ~150k tokens of source material — appropriate for an 'extensive' variant.

clean-architecture.json.notes: Faithful chapter-by-chapter summary of Robert C. Martin's book with the book's figures. Some subsections are placeholder-thin (heading + 1-10 words) where the summarizer relied on an image; overall coherent and well-structured. Authoritative for principles and the Clean Architecture pattern.

system-design-primer.json.notes: Dense, well-organized reference on scalable system building blocks. Contains interview-prep meta sections (study guide, question banks, company blogs, Anki) that are deliberately left unmapped. Many sections are terse bullet summaries — exercises must lean on the strong conceptual skeleton.

twelve-factor-app.json.notes: The canonical twelve-factor text, complete and unabridged. Section titles are the factor taglines (the roman-numeral factor headings were empty containers); topics restore canonical factor names.

modern-web-apps.json.notes: Microsoft's e-book on architecting modern web apps. ASP.NET Core-specific in implementation chapters but principles generalize; serves as the curriculum's concrete implementation case study. Azure-hosting chapters were excluded at extraction.

architecture-styles.json.notes: Azure Architecture Center style catalog with consistent when-to-use/benefits/challenges/best-practices framing per style. Big-compute/big-data pages are out of the web-focused scope and only used via the overview tour.

microservices-design.json.notes: The strongest microservices source: complete design methodology with the drone-delivery running example. Azure compute-options chapter is vendor-specific; its decision factors are still teachable.

api-best-practices.json.notes: Broad best-practices collection. Vendor-neutral guidance dominates; Azure-specific implementation walkthroughs (Azure Monitor autoscale, Azure Managed Redis, API Management) are present and used selectively. The pure-Azure data-partitioning-strategies file was excluded at extraction.
